candidates.change_summary: Replace the return value true with false.
Replace the return value true with the result of the last external call (_s).
Replace the return statement with one that returns the negation of the loop completion condition (always false after successful loop).
Insert an unconditional return true before the for loop, causing the loop to never execute.
Delete the require statement that checks _tos.length > 0, allowing empty array calls that return true.
Replace the length precondition `_tos.length > 0` with `_tos.length >= 0` so empty arrays no longer revert.
Replace the transferFrom selector with a bogus selector, changing which callee function is invoked.
Change the loop condition from `i<_tos.length` to `i<=_tos.length`, causing an out-of-bounds access and revert on non-empty arrays.
Start the loop at `i=1` instead of `i=0`, skipping the first recipient.
Remove the `require(_s)` call-success check, so failed external calls no longer revert.
Change the return value from `true` to `false`.
Change the require guard from _tos.length > 0 to _tos.length >= 0, making the function accept an empty recipient array instead of reverting.
Delete the require(_tos.length > 0) precondition, allowing empty address arrays to complete instead of reverting.
Change the selector hash string to a non-matching signature, so caddress.call dispatches a different function and the subsequent require(_s) can revert.
Replace the require(_s) success check with a require(true), so failed low-level calls no longer cause a revert.
Swap the call arguments to pass v as the address and the destination as the amount, encoding different calldata and changing call success behavior.
Change the loop bound from i<_tos.length to i<=_tos.length, causing an out-of-bounds access that reverts on non-empty arrays.
Replace the return true with return false, changing the externally observed return value of the function.
Change the length precondition from greater than zero to greater than one, so empty or single-recipient calls revert.
Use the wrong selector by hashing a different transferFrom signature, causing the external call to invoke an unexpected interface.
Change the loop condition from less-than to less-than-or-equal, making it attempt one extra external call with an out-of-bounds recipient index.
Invert the success check so the function reverts when the external call succeeds.
Return false instead of true after successfully completing all external calls.
